explain.say: When you rotate a photo on your phone, every single dot of it moves. A matrix is the recipe that tells each dot where to go. Look at the first stage: a grid of points, each with an x and a y.

explain.say: Here is the secret. The first column of the matrix says where the point 1, 0 lands. For a quarter-turn rotation, the first column is 0, 1. So 1, 0 swings up to 0, 1. See the second stage?

faq.q: What does a matrix do to a point?
faq.a: It moves it. A 2 by 2 matrix sends the point x, y to x times the first column plus y times the second column.
asks: How do you multiply a matrix by a point?

faq.q: What do the columns of a matrix mean?
faq.a: The first column is where the point 1, 0 lands, and the second column is where 0, 1 lands. Those two landing spots decide where everything else goes.

faq.q: How does a rotation matrix work?
faq.a: For a quarter turn anticlockwise, 1, 0 goes to 0, 1 and 0, 1 goes to minus 1, 0. So the matrix has columns 0, 1 and minus 1, 0.
asks: What is the matrix for a 90 degree rotation?

faq.q: Why do straight lines stay straight?
faq.a: A matrix moves points by mixing the two columns in proportion. Evenly spaced points on a line stay evenly spaced on a new line. That is called a linear transformation.

faq.q: What matrix leaves everything where it is?
faq.a: The identity matrix, with columns 1, 0 and 0, 1. It sends every point back to itself.

facts: The columns of a 2×2 matrix are the images of the points (1, 0) and (0, 1).
The matrix with columns (0, 1) and (−1, 0) rotates the plane 90° anticlockwise about the origin.

quiz.say: A matrix has columns (3, 0) and (0, 3). What does it do?
quiz.show: A matrix has columns (3, 0) and (0, 3). What does it do?
quiz.why: (1, 0) goes to (3, 0) and (0, 1) goes to (0, 3): everything is 3 times further from the origin.

wrong.0: A rotation would swing (1, 0) round, not stretch it.
wrong.1: A reflection in the x-axis would send (0, 1) to (0, −1).

quiz.say: Using the quarter turn matrix, where does the point 1, 3 go?
quiz.show: Using the quarter-turn matrix, where does (1, 3) go?

wrong.1: (3, 1) swaps the numbers but forgets the minus sign.
wrong.2: (1, −3) is a reflection in the x-axis.
